title: Black Light FTL Installation Safety Timing and Readiness Registry
purpose: Translate named installation sensor, control, actuation, maintenance and recovery evidence into provenance-bearing timing modifiers without inventing canonical seconds, transit-family identity, or universal race coefficients.

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Sensor lookahead, emergency de-transit, family-specific safety margins, failure sensitivity, and the principle that more advanced systems reduce risk without making transit perfectly safe.

mathematicalModel.baselineIntervention: t_int,0 = t_sensor + t_solver + t_decision + t_command + t_actuate + t_exit + t_clear + t_margin
mathematicalModel.readinessRange: 0 < r_i <= 1 for certified operation; r_i <= 0 blocks use of that channel rather than producing infinite or negative time
mathematicalModel.maintenancePenalty: m_i >= 1 is a multiplicative degradation factor derived from measured condition or explicitly PROPOSED simulation calibration
mathematicalModel.lookaheadScaling: t_prediction = t_prediction,0 * r_sensor * r_navigation * r_reference / m_prediction
mathematicalModel.continuousMargin: M_T = D_B/v_progress - t_int for continuous projected-progress families where v_progress has an authoritative route-progress semantic
mathematicalModel.precommitMargin: M_T = t_prediction - t_int for PRECOMMIT families; no intermediate local FTL velocity may be fabricated
mathematicalModel.interpretation: Readiness changes the installation's ability to observe, decide, actuate and recover. It does not alter G, the external tidal tensor, or the underlying family equations.

records.timingPolicy: Use the route-safety baseline timing unchanged when no narrower sourced readiness record is available. Runtime condition measurements may still reduce readiness, but generic identity alone contributes no invented bonus.

derivedTimingImplications: sensor, control and recovery paths may be distributed through cultivated neural, vibratory, ionic, optical or biological carriers
biological state inhomogeneity, damage isolation, tissue viability and coordination span are relevant timing/readiness dimensions
a repaired biological component requires recalibration before it can be assumed to have restored timing authority
records.numericPolicy: No canonical Ar'nock sensor latency, solver latency, actuation latency, exit time, recovery reserve or family-specific coefficient is currently established. Do not auto-apply numeric bonuses or penalties from race identity alone.

confirmedEvidence: Gravitic Slipstream Regulator with flexible field vanes immersed in dielectric fluid
Navigation Current Well encoding vector, gravity and transit risk
Forward Sensor Ampulla for long-baseline observation and ranging
Sensor Choir Alcove for multimodal sensor fusion
asymmetric vane response can rotate the local inertial frame
records.numericPolicy: The source establishes which machinery states matter but not canonical seconds. Runtime may map measured readiness fractions into timing penalties using the generic equations; source identity alone supplies no invented absolute latency.
records.familyFirewall: The source term 'bio-reactive gravitic slipstream system' remains unresolved against consolidated family IDs. Timing/readiness evidence must not select gravitational-plane or slipstream-shear by keyword.

runtimeRules: Narrower matching scope outranks broader scope; equal-precedence contradictions return CONFLICT rather than averaging.
UNRESOLVED named records preserve their evidence but do not create numeric timing modifiers.
Measured readiness may only worsen or preserve a baseline unless a sourced named record explicitly provides a certified improvement factor.
A zero or negative readiness channel is a blocking condition, not a division-by-zero workaround.
Maintenance state affects timing/readiness and recovery authority; it does not change external gravity or transit-family identity.
Named technology, vessel, installation, manufacturer or race identity is never a family selector.
PRECOMMIT families remain timing-based and may not be assigned a fabricated local transit velocity.
Protected recovery reserve may not be consumed to improve advertised nominal timing.
All adjusted timing packets must preserve baseline values, applied factors, source record IDs and provenance.
canonGuards: No absolute timing number in this registry is historical or universal canon unless a named source explicitly says so.
The Ar'nock record does not establish a transit family or canonical timing performance.
The Mur'rek record establishes machinery dependencies but not a normalized FTL family or canonical timing in seconds.
Readiness equations are engineering models, not evidence that a fictional hazard exists.
Race/species identity may constrain machinery embodiment but may not create family identity, manufacturer identity, or performance canon.
Simulation calibration must remain labeled PROPOSED or DERIVED as applicable.
